mechanism.statement: Seat revocation closed every DURABLE door and left the live sink attached, so a removed participant who did not disconnect kept receiving campaign-scoped committed facts.
beforeTheFix: src/lib/multiplayer/server/CampaignSyncSession.ts:362-376 (pre-fix numbering) - attachLiveParticipant returned this.host.subscribe(...)'s unsubscribe directly; the session held no participant-keyed index of live attachments, so the removal path structurally COULD NOT detach.

src/lib/multiplayer/server/bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:881-896 - applyCommittedParticipantRemovals calls membership?.revoke(...) then entry.syncSession.applyCommittedParticipantRemoval(event), and nothing else. The unsubscribe lives in that socket's own cleanupFns and runs on DISCONNECT only.

Why deleting from `retained` stopped nothing: the launch gate that reads `retained` is documented at CampaignSyncSession.ts (evaluateScenarioLaunch header) as 'deliberately not consulted anywhere on the delivery path'. `retained` is convergence bookkeeping; it never was the delivery gate.

everyLiveAttachIsIdentified.claim: every production attach passes a proven participantId, so a participant-keyed index covers all of them
callSites: bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:1028 durable-member rejoin arm - joinMember(sink, verifiedPlayerId)
bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:1108 resync arm - resyncGuest(lastSeq, sink, verifiedPlayerId)
bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:1162 room-code newcomer arm - joinGuest(roomCode, sink, verifiedPlayerId)

otherCommittedRemovalPaths.asked: grep for every caller of applyCommittedParticipantRemoval
otherCommittedRemovalPaths.found: exactly one, bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:894, reached from two places: the live command path (:834, applied from the committed batch in hand) and healCommittedParticipantRemovals (:878, which re-walks EVERY committed removal before admission on later frames). Both go through the same drain, and the heal pass is why the method's idempotence is load-bearing.
otherCommittedRemovalPaths.consequence: no second drain site was needed

fix.shape: a participant-keyed index of live detaches on the session, drained by the committed removal
postFixLines: :208 - `private readonly liveByParticipant = new Map<string, Set<() => void>>();`, declared beside `retained` with the comment stating why they are different things.

:385-416 - attachLiveParticipant now names the host.subscribe unsubscribe, returns it unchanged for an UNIDENTIFIED sink (nothing could ever name it, so a row for it could never be drained), and for an identified one registers a `detach` wrapper that deregisters itself (:408-412) before unsubscribing, then returns the wrapper.

:694-706 - applyCommittedParticipantRemoval keeps `this.retained.delete(participantId)` and then drains `liveByParticipant.get(participantId)` via `for (const detach of Array.from(attached)) detach();` (:704) before deleting the key (:705). Array.from rather than a spread because tsconfig target is es5 and the spread trips TS2802 - measured, see gates.tsc.firstRun.
fix.setNotSingleFunction: the same participant can legitimately hold more than one live attachment at a time (second tab, or a reconnect landing before the old socket's close is processed - the case `gmConnections` already counts for the GM); keeping only the newest would leave the older one delivering.
fix.wrapperRationale: without self-deregistration the socket's own cleanupFns would leave a dead entry for every closed connection, so the map would grow across reconnects. Behaviourally harmless (see mutant c) - kept for leak control.
fix.idempotence: draining a missing key returns early, preserving the documented contract that a recovery pass can re-apply the same removal.
fix.deliberatelyNotDone: sending the revoked socket a typed close. CampaignSyncSession holds SINKS, not sockets, so it can stop delivering and cannot emit closeTyped(AUTH_REJECTED,'membership-revoked'). That needs a participant-keyed socket index in bindCampaignSyncConnection (socketsByMatch is keyed by matchId only) and an owner decision on whether a removed member is disconnected or merely goes quiet. The removed member's connection goes quiet and is refused by name on its next authenticated frame.

table.mutation: forget deregistration on disconnect - detach becomes `() => unsubscribe()`, so a closed socket's entry stays in the set and a later removal drains it a second time
table.verdict: SURVIVES - and the brief anticipated this ('must be harmless or pinned'). It is HARMLESS at the behavioural surface, for a reason read at source this session: CampaignMatchHost.subscribe (CampaignMatchHost.ts:262-267) returns `() => { this.subscribers.delete(subscriber); }`, a Set delete, so calling it twice is a no-op. A stale entry drained a second time therefore changes nothing for any viewer. What the deregistration actually buys is LEAK CONTROL - without it `liveByParticipant` accumulates one dead entry per closed connection for the life of the session - and that is memory, not behaviour, so it is not assertable without exposing session internals. Stated rather than pinned; see openQuestions.

killedBy: bindCampaignSyncConnection 'revokes the durable seat, detaches the live player, and unblocks the next launch'

THE REVOKED SOCKET IS NOT CLOSED, only silenced. No typed AUTH_REJECTED/'membership-revoked' close frame is sent to an already-bound socket - see fix.deliberatelyNotDone. A removed member's connection stays open and mute until they disconnect or send their next authenticated frame, which is refused by name (bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:934-939).
GRANT revocation (task 4.3) is a different subsystem and was neither changed nor re-measured here. This slice is about SEAT revocation, which is what /activity and the rejoin gate read.

openQuestions.question: Should a removed member's socket be CLOSED with AUTH_REJECTED/'membership-revoked' rather than merely going quiet?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: A silent socket looks identical to an idle campaign from the client's side, so a removed player sees a frozen screen rather than a reason. The rejoin path already has the typed refusal, so the vocabulary exists.
openQuestions.whyNotDoneHere: CampaignSyncSession holds sinks, not sockets; the close needs a participant-keyed socket index in bindCampaignSyncConnection (socketsByMatch is keyed by matchId only). That is a strictly larger change and an owner decision, not a minimal fix.

openQuestions.question: Is a growing `liveByParticipant` worth an assertable surface (e.g. a test-only size accessor), or is the argument enough?
openQuestions.context: mutant c survives because a double drain is harmless; the only thing the self-deregistration protects is map growth across reconnects, which no row can see today.
